mainTopic: The two dippings at the סדר: whether מצוות need כוונה, what the two cooked dishes are, and the ברכות on the מרור
overview: The משנה says that at the סדר, חזרת is dipped and eaten before the מצה and then eaten again later as מרור. ריש לקיש learns from this that מצוות צריכות כוונה: the first eating does not count because the person was not thinking of the מצוה. The גמרא offers another reason for the two dippings, היכירא לתינוקות, which is a way to make the children ask. It also brings a ברייתא saying that one who ate מרור without intent is יוצא. The גמרא answers that תנאים argue about this: רבי יוסי calls the second חזרת a 'מצוה', which shows he requires כוונה. Next the גמרא asks what the 'two cooked dishes' are. רב הונא says beets and rice, and from this רב אשי learns that nobody holds rice can become חמץ. חזקיה, רב יוסף and רבינא give other options. Finally, רב הונא rules that when only lettuce is available, one says בורא פרי האדמה on it at the first dipping and על אכילת מרור on it after the מצה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש‎: מצוות require intent
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the משנה shows that מצוות צריכות כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: ריש לקיש said: This teaches that מצוות require intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with ריש לקיש, who draws a general rule from our משנה: to fulfill a מצוה you must intend to do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only describes the order of the סדר, with חזרת dipped twice. ריש לקיש says this detail reveals a big principle that applies to all מצוות. The next steps explain how he gets there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is to say': a formula for drawing a rule out of a source
מצוות require intent to fulfill the obligation
Intent: consciously meaning to do the מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether מצוות צריכות כוונה is one of the most famous questions in all of ש״ס. It affects every מצוה a person does.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Reish Lakish said:
This is to say (this teaches)
that מצוות require intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצוות צריכות כוונה: a מצוה done without intent does not count.

steps.title: Why the first eating of lettuce does not count
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the first eating of חזרת was done as a vegetable, not as מרור, so it must be dipped again for מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he does not eat it at the time of the obligation of מרור, he eats it with the blessing בורא פרי האדמה. Perhaps he did not intend it for מרור, so he needs to dip it again for the sake of מרור.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש lays out the case in the משנה: the first eating of חזרת happens before the time of the מרור obligation, with only a בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At that first eating, the person thinks of it as an ordinary vegetable, not as מרור. So maybe he had no כוונה for מרור, and that is why the משנה requires a second dipping meant for מרור.

keyTerms.meaning: Bitter herbs eaten at the סדר

phrases.english: Since it is not at the time
of the obligation of maror that he eats it,
with 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
is how he eats it.
And perhaps he did not intend it for maror,
therefore he needs to go back
and dip it for the sake of maror.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how ריש לקיש reads the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה requiring a second dipping of חזרת for מרור

steps.title: Otherwise, why dip twice?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes his proof: if intent were not needed, the first dipping would already count, and a second would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think a מצוה does not require intent, why do you need two dippings? He already dipped it once!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש closes his argument by showing what goes wrong if you hold the opposite view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a כוונה requirement, the person already ate חזרת, which is valid מרור, at the first dipping. So the משנה's second dipping only makes sense if the first eating failed for lack of כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it should enter your mind: introduces a rejected assumption

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's whole proof rests on one question: why would the משנה need two dippings unless the first one failed for lack of כוונה?

phrases.english: For if it should enter your mind
that a מצוה does not require intent,
why do you need two dippings?
But he already dipped it once!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מִצְוָה לָא בָּעֲיָא כַּוּוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 2 by showing the alternative makes no sense
steps.raayaSupportSource: The otherwise unexplained second dipping in the משנה

steps.title: Maybe two dippings are for the children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: maybe intent is not required, and the two dippings exist to make the children curious.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know? Perhaps מצוות actually do not require intent. As for your question, 'why do I need two dippings?', it is so that there will be something unusual for the children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש by offering a different reason for the second dipping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש assumed the only possible reason for two dippings was a missing כוונה. The גמרא says there could be an educational reason: doing something unusual (היכירא) makes children ask questions. If so, the משנה proves nothing about כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not ruling here that מצוות אין צריכות כוונה. It is only showing that the משנה can be read without that rule, so ריש לקיש's proof is not conclusive.

phrases.english: From where (do you know this)?
Perhaps: actually
מצוות do not require intent,
and as for what you said, 'why do I need two dippings?'
it is so that there will be
something noticeable for the children.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא: לְעוֹלָם מִצְוֹת אֵין צְרִיכוֹת כַּוּוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3 by offering another explanation
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not necessarily ריש לקיש's rule itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the only reason for two dippings is a lack of כוונה, but היכירא לתינוקות also explains it

steps.title: Then why not use other vegetables?
steps.stepSummary: A challenge to the children explanation: if the point is just to make the children curious, the משנה should have used other vegetables for the first dipping.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: If so, let the משנה teach us about other vegetables!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to its own explanation. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two dippings are only for the children, any vegetable would work for the first dipping. Why does the משנה describe dipping חזרת, the מרור itself? That choice seems to suggest the first eating was meant as מרור, which brings back ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say: introduces an anticipated objection

phrases.english: And if you say:
If so, let it teach us about other vegetables?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא: אִם כֵּן לַישְׁמְעִינַן שְׁאָר יְרָקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the היכירא לתינוקות explanation of step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that two dippings exist for the children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the aim is just an unusual sign, the משנה's choice of חזרת for the first dipping is unexplained

steps.title: Even with only lettuce, dip twice
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה chose חזרת to teach that even someone who has only חזרת must still dip twice for the children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Had it taught us about other vegetables, I would have said: only where there are other vegetables do we need two dippings, but with lettuce alone we do not. So it teaches us that even with lettuce we need two dippings, so there will be something noticeable for the children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and defends the children explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה had mentioned other vegetables, we might think two dippings apply only when you have two kinds of vegetables. By using חזרת, the משנה teaches a bigger point: even with just one vegetable you dip twice. So the choice of חזרת fits the children explanation well.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought: an initial mistaken assumption

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא can explain the double dipping without needing ריש לקיש's rule, so the משנה does not prove that מצוות צריכות כוונה.

phrases.english: If it had taught us other vegetables,
I would have said:
where there are other vegetables
is when we require two dippings,
but lettuce alone
does not require two dippings,
so it teaches us
that even lettuce requires two dippings,
so that there will be in it
something noticeable for the children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן שְׁאָר יְרָקוֹת, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording of the משנה: why it chose חזרת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two dippings are needed only when there are two different vegetables
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with חזרת alone, dip twice for היכירא לתינוקות

steps.title: ברייתא: eating without intent still counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: one who ate מרור that was דמאי, without intent, or in halves has fulfilled the מצוה. This seems to say outright that intent is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it was taught: If he ate them as דמאי, he fulfilled his obligation. If he ate them without intent, he fulfilled his obligation. If he ate them in halves, he fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a stronger point against ריש לקיש: a ברייתא that seems to say directly that מרור eaten without intent still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אכלן בלא מתכוין יצא appears to contradict ריש לקיש's rule that מצוות צריכות כוונה. The ברייתא also allows eating doubtfully tithed produce (דמאי) and eating in two half-portions. The ברייתא finishes in the next step, and step 9 gives the answer: this is an argument among תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat this ברייתא as the final word on כוונה. The גמרא does not reinterpret 'without intent'. Instead, it answers that the question is an argument among תנאים (step 9), so ריש לקיש can follow a different תנא.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught (in a baraita):
If he ate them as demai, he fulfilled his obligation.
If he ate them without intent, he fulfilled his obligation.
If he ate them in halves, he fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes beyond the rejection in step 4 by citing a source that seems to oppose ריש לקיש directly
steps.raayaObject: מצוות אין צריכות כוונה, against ריש לקיש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: אכלן בלא מתכוין יצא

steps.title: The ברייתא's last condition and the challenge to ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a condition: the two halves of מרור only join together if the pause between them is no longer than כדי אכילת פרס. The ברייתא as a whole, which says that eating without כוונה counts, now stands as a challenge to ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as he does not wait between one eating and the next longer than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step and adds one condition about eating the מרור in two halves. The exclamation mark signals that the whole ברייתא is now being thrown at ריש לקיש as a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only limits the 'halves' case: the two half-portions join only if they are eaten within כדי אכילת פרס. The real challenge comes from the earlier part of the ברייתא. It said that one who ate מרור without כוונה is יוצא, while ריש לקיש holds that מצוות need כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: The time it takes to eat a half-loaf; the time limit for joining two eatings into one

steps.confusionAlert: The time-limit condition is not itself the challenge. It only applies to the 'halves' case. The challenge to ריש לקיש comes from the words 'without כוונה' earlier in the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: Provided that he does not pause
between one eating and the next
phrases.notes: Between the first half-olive and the second half-olive

phrases.english: more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf!
phrases.notes: This is a challenge: the ברייתא seems to go against ריש לקיש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁהֶא בֵּין אֲכִילָה לַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 7, which now works as a challenge to ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that מצוות need כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly says that one who ate מרור without כוונה is יוצא. That contradicts the need for כוונה.

steps.title: It is an argument among תנאים; רבי יוסי requires a second dipping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whether מצוות need כוונה is an argument among תנאים. רבי יוסי says that even after dipping חזרת, it is a מצוה to bring חזרת again. That suggests the first eating did not count, because it lacked כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is an argument among תנאים. As it was taught: רבי יוסי says, even though he already dipped the lettuce, it is a מצוה to bring before him lettuce, חרוסת, and two cooked dishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. The ברייתא is not the only voice: other תנאים, like רבי יוסי, seem to agree that כוונה is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not have to follow the earlier ברייתא, because he can side with another תנא. רבי יוסי says to bring חזרת again even after one already dipped it. That only makes sense if the first eating did not count, since it was done without כוונה for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument among תנאים
The sweet dip used at the סדר
Two cooked dishes; which foods they are is debated in steps 12-18

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ריש לקיש's view has a source among the תנאים, so one opposing ברייתא does not knock it down.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim.
As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even though he already dipped the lettuce,
it is a מצוה to bring before him
lettuce, charoses, and two cooked dishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by showing that תנאים argue about this question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute of תנאים: ריש לקיש follows a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that everyone holds כוונה is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: תנאים argue. רבי יוסי seems to require כוונה, and ריש לקיש can follow him.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי's second dipping is just for the children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the proof from רבי יוסי. Perhaps he holds that מצוות do not need כוונה, and the second dipping is only there to make the children notice and ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, from where do you know? Perhaps רבי יוסי holds that מצוות do not need intent, and the reason we need two dippings is so there will be something noticeable for the children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the claim that רבי יוסי requires כוונה. It offers the same 'for the children' explanation that we saw earlier in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second dipping could have a reason that has nothing to do with כוונה: getting the children to ask questions. If so, רבי יוסי no longer supports ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: And still, from where do we know this?
Something noticeable, a sign that makes the children ask

phrases.english: And still, from where do you know?
Perhaps Rabbi Yosei holds
that מצוות do not need intent,
and the reason we need two dippings
is so there will be something noticeable for the children.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of רבי יוסי used in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי יוסי requires כוונה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The second dipping could be explained by the children's reason instead of a need for כוונה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי calls it a מצוה, so it cannot just be for the children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the 'children' explanation. רבי יוסי uses the word 'מצוה', and that word fits eating מרור properly, not just catching the children's attention.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'מצוה'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the challenge from step 10 using one word in רבי יוסי's statement. That restores the proof that רבי יוסי requires כוונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting the children's attention is not described as a 'מצוה' to bring חזרת. Since רבי יוסי calls the second חזרת a מצוה, the second eating must be the real מצוה of מרור. So the first eating did not count, because it lacked כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A commandment; here, the real obligation of eating מרור

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי holds that מצוות need כוונה, so ריש לקיש has a תנא to rely on against the ברייתא that says one who ate without כוונה is יוצא.

phrases.english: If so, what is the meaning of 'מצוה'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'children' explanation of step 10 from the wording 'מצוה'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second dipping might only be for the children.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'מצוה' shows the second eating is the real מצוה, so רבי יוסי requires כוונה.

steps.title: What are the two cooked dishes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the 'two cooked dishes' are.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the two cooked dishes?
steps.whatsHappening: The כוונה discussion is over, and the גמרא now asks a side question to clarify a term. This sets up רב הונא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two cooked dishes' were mentioned in רבי יוסי's ברייתא, and in the משנה. The גמרא wants to know which foods are meant.

phrases.english: What are the two cooked dishes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כוונה topic to define a term from the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which foods count as the two cooked dishes

steps.title: רב הונא: beets and rice
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the two cooked dishes can be beets and rice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: beets and rice.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question from the last step by naming two foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא shows that the two cooked dishes do not have to be meat. Even simple cooked foods like beets and rice are enough.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: beets and rice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two cooked dishes can be beets and rice.

steps.title: רבא would seek out beets and rice because רב הונא said it
steps.stepSummary: רבא made a point of getting beets and rice for the סדר, because these foods had been named by רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would seek out beets and rice, since it came out of the mouth of רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about רבא's practice that follows from רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא may only have been giving examples, and any two cooked foods would work. Still, רבא wanted to follow his teacher's exact words. This shows how much he respected his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: Would seek out / make an effort to get

steps.whatToRemember: The two cooked dishes can be simple foods like beets and rice. רבא made a point of using exactly these because his teacher רב הונא named them.

phrases.english: Rava would seek out
beets and rice,
since it came out of the mouth of Rav Huna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבא put רב הונא's answer into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא made a point of using beets and rice as the two cooked dishes, out of respect for רב הונא's words.

steps.title: רב אשי learns that nobody follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי on rice
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reasons from רב הונא's ruling that rice may be one of the cooked dishes. He concludes that no one worries about רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view that rice is a real grain that can become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Learn from רב הונא that no one is concerned about the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says that rice is a type of grain. A person who eats it as חמץ is liable to כרת, and a person can fulfill his obligation of מצה with it on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי draws a side lesson from רב הונא's statement in Step 13. Because רב הונא allowed cooked rice at the סדר, it seems no one treats rice as a grain that can become חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain cooked in water can become חמץ. If רב הונא thought rice was a real grain, he would never have suggested cooking it on פסח night. So רב הונא clearly does not follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and רב אשי takes this to mean that nobody follows him in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (an inference drawn from a statement)
There is no one who is concerned about (this view)
A type of grain (one of the grains that can become חמץ)
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating חמץ on פסח

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view goes both ways. Rice can become חמץ (a stringency), and rice can also be used for מצה (a leniency). רב אשי's inference comes from the חמץ side: cooking rice would be forbidden if rice could become חמץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the rule that rice is not one of the five grains for the laws of חמץ and מצה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Learn from this statement of Rav Huna
phrases.notes: Refers to רב הונא's ruling that beets and rice can be the two cooked dishes

phrases.english: that there is no one who is concerned about that
statement of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
Rice is a type of grain,
and one is liable to karet for eating it in its leavened state,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בּוֹ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: and a person fulfills his obligation with it on Passover.
phrases.notes: That is, he fulfills the obligation of מצה with מצה made from rice

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא, לֵית דְּחָיֵישׁ לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side halachic inference from רב הונא's answer about rice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since רב הונא allows cooked rice on פסח, rice is not treated as a grain that can become חמץ, against רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

steps.title: חזקיה: fish and the egg on it can count
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the two cooked dishes may even be a fish and the egg cooked on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The two cooked dishes may even be a fish and the egg that is on it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another option for the two cooked dishes. He accepts even a fish with egg smeared or fried on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two 'dishes' are really one food item with a coating. חזקיה holds that this still counts as two separate cooked foods, which makes the requirement easy to meet.

keyTerms.meaning: The egg that is on it (egg cooked onto the fish)

phrases.english: Chizkiya said:
Even a fish and the egg that is on it.
phrases.notes: That is, an egg fried or smeared onto the fish

steps.triggerLanguage: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ דָּג וּבֵיצָה שֶׁעָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than רב הונא to the question of what the two cooked dishes are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish with egg cooked on it can count as the two cooked dishes.

steps.title: רב יוסף: two kinds of meat, for the פסח and the חגיגה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף requires two kinds of meat. One recalls the קרבן פסח, and the other recalls the קרבן חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: One needs two kinds of meat. One is a reminder of the קרבן פסח, and the other is a reminder of the קרבן חגיגה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a stricter view. The two dishes must be two kinds of meat, and he explains what each one stands for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף gives the reason behind the two dishes. In the בית המקדש, two offerings were eaten on פסח night: the קרבן פסח and the קרבן חגיגה. Because the dishes recall meat offerings, he holds they must be meat, not beets, rice, or fish.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival peace-offering eaten together with the קרבן פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the custom of putting two cooked items on the סדר plate (the זרוע and the ביצה) as reminders of the two offerings.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
One needs two kinds of meat,
one as a remembrance of the Paschal offering,
and one as a remembrance of the Festival offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: צָרִיךְ שְׁנֵי מִינֵי בָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to what the two cooked dishes are. It also adds the reason for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two cooked dishes must be two kinds of meat, recalling the קרבן פסח and the קרבן חגיגה.

steps.title: רבינא: even meat on the bone and its gravy
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that even a bone with meat and the gravy it was cooked in can count as the two dishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Even a bone with meat and its cooking gravy can count.
steps.whatsHappening: A final אמורא gives the most lenient option. One piece of meat on the bone plus the liquid it cooked in is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא seems to accept רב יוסף's idea that meat recalls the offerings. Still, he does not require two separate kinds of meat. Meat and its own gravy are treated as two foods.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on the two cooked dishes: beets and rice (רב הונא), fish and egg (חזקיה), two kinds of meat for the פסח and חגיגה (רב יוסף), and a bone with its gravy (רבינא).

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Even a bone and the cooked gravy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last opinion in the list about the two cooked dishes. It is more lenient than רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat on the bone and its gravy can count as the two cooked dishes.

steps.title: The obvious case: other vegetables are available
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that when other vegetables are available, one makes בורא פרי האדמה on them first. Later, one makes על אכילת מרור on the מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: where there are other vegetables, one makes בורא פרי האדמה over the other vegetables and eats them. Then one makes על אכילת מרור and eats the מרור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes topic to the ברכות over vegetables. It starts with the simple case, which sets up the harder question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two different vegetables are available, each ברכה has its own vegetable. בורא פרי האדמה goes on the first dipping, and that ברכה also covers the מרור eaten later. על אכילת מרור goes on the מרור itself. The real question is what to do when only one vegetable is available.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה over produce that grows from the ground
The מצוה ברכה over eating bitter herbs

phrases.english: It is obvious
that where there are other vegetables,
one recites over the other vegetables
'Who creates the fruit of the ground' and eats,
and then he recites
'Over eating bitter herbs' and eats.
phrases.notes: Recited at the second dipping, over the lettuce

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the order of ברכות over vegetables. It is the setup for the question that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With other vegetables available, make בורא פרי האדמה on them first, and על אכילת מרור later on the מרור.

steps.title: What if only lettuce is available?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to make the ברכות when the only vegetable is lettuce, the same vegetable used for מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there is only lettuce, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the real question that the obvious case was setting up. It wants to know the order of ברכות when only one vegetable is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the same lettuce has to be used for both dippings. It is unclear when each ברכה should be said, and whether על אכילת מרור belongs at the first eating or the second.

phrases.english: Where there is only lettuce, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious case to the case that is actually unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When to say בורא פרי האדמה and when to say על אכילת מרור if lettuce is the only vegetable.

steps.title: רב הונא: first בורא פרי האדמה, later על אכילת מרור, both on the lettuce
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that at the first dipping one says בורא פרי האדמה over the lettuce. At the end, one says על אכילת מרור over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: At the beginning, one says בורא פרי האדמה over the מרור and eats it. At the end, one says על אכילת מרור over it and eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. The lettuce is eaten twice, with a different ברכה each time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first eating is treated as an ordinary vegetable, so it gets only בורא פרי האדמה. The second eating, after the מצה, is the real מצוה of מרור, so על אכילת מרור is said then.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not say על אכילת מרור at the first eating, even though it is the same lettuce. The מצוה ברכה waits for the second eating.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One initially recites over the bitter herbs
'Who creates the fruit of the ground' and eats,
and ultimately he recites over it
'Over eating bitter herbs' and eats.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מְבָרֵךְ מֵעִיקָּרָא אַמָּרוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First dipping: בורא פרי האדמה on the lettuce. Later, after the מצה: על אכילת מרור on the lettuce.
